Source: api/rest/src/PublicApiRuntime.cpp, platformCapabilities(). Each availability value depends on configured runtime services. Available here does not mean an individual actor has permission or that the installed TV integration has passed acceptance.

get.summary: List backend identities visible to the authenticated actor
get.description: Source: api/rest/src/PublicApiRuntime.cpp, parsePublicBackendCollectionQuery()/publicBackendCollectionResponse(), and core/security/include/SecurityHttpGate.h. An authenticated actor is mandatory; visibility is derived from positive permission-grant backend scopes, not a new backends.view permission. role.read-only alone does not contribute scope. Authenticated users with no positive backend scopes receive an empty 200 collection. The exact authentication transport is deployment-dependent and is not expressed here as a single invented HTTP security scheme (see x-vdr-suite-authentication). A query cursor is opaque (currently be1_-prefixed) and bound to the normalized authorization scope. Restart pagination on 409 cursor_expired; never synthesize or parse cursors. Success responses include Cache-Control: no-store and do not include ETag. Other HTTP methods, including HEAD/OPTIONS, return 405 method_not_allowed with Allow: GET.

x-vdr-suite-authentication.authorization: Positive permission grants determine visible backend scopes; no backends.view permission exists.
x-vdr-suite-authentication.securitySchemeDocumentation: See ADR-0048, security gate and deployment identity configuration; credential transport is not fully modeled in this partial OpenAPI.

503.description: Permission resolution, collection runtime or its validated output is unavailable; code may depend on rejection layer.

get.summary: List Channels from explicitly selected and authorized VDR backends
get.description: An authenticated actor must provide 1–16 distinct backendId query members. Each requested source is independently authorized with channels.view@backend; one denial rejects the entire request, before collection evaluation. The order is (backendId ASC, channelId ASC). The opaque ch1_-prefixed cursor binds the normalized backend source set and last item; source-set mismatch returns 409 cursor_expired. A 200 response may be partial: meta.sources gives all requested sources, and unavailable sources are not silently hidden. At least one source must succeed for a 200; all unavailable yields 503 backend_unavailable. The response has Cache-Control: no-store and no collection ETag. No legacy /api/vdr/channels fallback is permitted by this contract.

x-vdr-suite-authentication.authorization: channels.view for every explicitly requested backendId
x-vdr-suite-authentication.securitySchemeDocumentation: Deployment authentication transports are not yet fully modeled in this partial OpenAPI; review the SecurityHttpGate and identity contracts.

parameters.name: backendId
parameters.description: Required repeated query key, 1–16 DISTINCT source IDs, e.g. ?backendId=backend-a&backendId=backend-b; omission does not select a default. Each ID 1–128 chars, alphanumeric, dot, underscore or hyphen.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of Channels returned per page; default 50.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned by page.nextCursor, source-set bound and nonportable across changed source scopes. Do not decode.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Exact required order of keyset fields.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Only ascending order is supported.

200.description: One or more sources succeeded. meta.partial may be true, with explicit per-source status and code.

partial.summary: One backend succeeded; another was unavailable

400.description: Missing, duplicated or invalid backend scope; invalid/unsupported query or malformed cursor. REST handler code invalid_request; security gate may return invalid_backend_scope.

403.description: One or more requested backends lack channels.view permission; no source results are disclosed.

409.description: Cursor backend source scope differs from selected source set; code cursor_expired.

503.description: All requested sources unavailable (backend_unavailable), or a required runtime/service/accountability layer is unavailable.

get.summary: List TimerAssignments from one authorized backend
get.description: Suite-owned durable collection; GET only. Requires timers.view for the backend query. Page order timerAssignmentId ASC; 50 default, maximum 100. Cursor is opaque, ta1_-prefixed in current implementation, bound to backend. A cursor from another backend is rejected as 400 invalid_request, not 409. The collection has no ETag, no native-VDR fallback or backend fanout, and meta.partial is always false. Authenticated scope is established by the security gate before the runtime handler.

get.summary: Read a backend-scoped TimerAssignment and its opaque ETag
get.description: Authenticated timers.view@backend. Public JSON does not expose assignmentRevision, native Timer data, state or scheduler internals. The ETag is a strong opaque encoding of durable revision; If-None-Match may return bodyless 304. No resource exists independently of backend authorization.

post.summary: Safely admit native Timer CREATE for an existing TimerAssignment
post.description: Protected mutation: authenticated actor and timers.create@backend are checked before existence disclosure. Browser-session CSRF applies where relevant. The backend is selected via query, not JSON. Must supply a canonical strong assignment If-Match plus an opaque Idempotency-Key; body is exactly {} (max 4096 bytes). A successful admission/replay returns 202 with Operation body/ETag/Location; it is NOT proof of successful native VDR Timer creation. No automatic retry after an uncertain result; any deliberate exact replay must retain the same scope, If-Match, key and request fingerprint. Server rechecks authorization/write policy even for replay.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Exactly one current canonical strong opaque TimerAssignment ETag from GET; no wildcard, list or weak tag.

parameters.description: Caller-chosen opaque visible ASCII key 1–160 bytes (0x21..0x7E); stable for explicit exact replay and never automatically regenerated on retry.

get.summary: Read the durable Operation owned by the authenticated actor
get.description: Item-only read; no /api/v1/operations collection. Exact actor ownership is checked in the read facade; other actors' Operation IDs and missing IDs both appear as 404. HTTP 200 means representation read, NOT mutation completion. State can be pending, terminal failure or uncertain (outcome_unknown). Strong opaque ETag and If-None-Match support conditional 304. No implicit polling, cancellation, backend fallback or automatic retry is part of the contract.
